oewn-00234667-r.learner: so as to move off from a certain thing, place, or position.
examples: The subject was pursued no further, and the gentlemen soon afterwards went away.
When Colonel Miller's regiment went away

oewn-00236283-r.learner: so that a thing stops being there at all.
examples: Four weeks were to pass away before her uncle and aunt's arrival.
It will pass away soon enough.

oewn-00236984-r.learner: at some distance from here in space, or at some distance from now in time.
examples: The village was two miles away.
Her birthday is still a month away.

oewn-00964479-v.learner: to trade thoughts with another person; to speak with someone.
examples: they continued talking together with mutual satisfaction till supper put an end to cards
"He did not talk to me of his own arts," said Fitzwilliam, smiling.
The child is only two years old and cannot talk yet.

oewn-00944022-v.learner: to put something into spoken words.
examples: He talks nonsense whenever he is nervous.

oewn-00167240-r.learner: for a great amount of time, or at a time far from now.
examples: she stayed with them only long enough to hear their favourable opinion of Bingley
shall hope to lead you to the altar ere long

oewn-00167533-r.learner: over a great amount of distance.
examples: He threw the ball long, well past everyone on the field.

oewn-03549540-n.learner: a building that one family or several families live in.
examples: The garden sloping to the road, the house standing in it, the green pales and the laurel hedge
No officer is ever to enter my house again, nor even to pass through the village.

oewn-08094856-n.learner: a group of people who live together.
examples: By ten o'clock the whole house had gone to bed.

oewn-03550330-n.learner: a building that keeps something inside it or holds it.
examples: They had a large carriage house behind the stables.

oewn-00038035-r.learner: in truth, and often used to make what you say stronger.
examples: The Lucases are very artful people, indeed, sister.
"I have heard, indeed, that she is uncommonly improved within this year or two."

oewn-00037864-r.learner: said on its own to show surprise, doubt, or the opposite of what the words say.
examples: "She refused him twice." "Indeed!"

connotation.why: can aim doubt or irony at what was just said

examples: You may possibly wonder why all this was not told you last night.

oewn-01016876-a.learner: coming after all the others in time, in place, or in degree, or being the only one left.
examples: She was the last to leave the room, and locked the door behind her.
He ate the last piece of bread on the plate.

oewn-01013868-s.learner: happening at the end of something, or making its end.
examples: The last scene of the play left the audience silent.

oewn-00017907-r.learner: used to make a point stronger, above all when what follows is something you would not expect.
examples: even Lydia was too much fatigued to utter more than the occasional exclamation
He even looked at her with a smile of affected incredulity.

oewn-00018101-r.learner: by a greater amount; used with words that compare.
examples: The second day was even colder than the first.

oewn-00018505-r.learner: used to say that something holds true in spite of the thing named.
examples: And even when it was settled that Lydia should go with Mrs. Forster, the necessity of opening her eyes to his character never occurred to me.

oewn-01830665-v.learner: to want something to happen and to look for it to happen.

it is said that he left Meryton greatly in debt: but I hope this may be false

oewn-00707813-v.learner: to mean to do something that you may well be able to do.
examples: was counting the days till she might reasonably hope to hear again

oewn-01815408-v.learner: to feel that things will turn out well; to be full of hope.
examples: There is nothing left to do now but wait and hope.

oewn-02208144-v.learner: to hold something, either a real thing you can touch or something you cannot.
examples: She was afraid of talking longer of his friend; and, having nothing else to say, was now determined to leave the trouble of finding a subject to him.

oewn-00772482-v.learner: to make someone or something do a thing, or act in a certain way.
examples: When my niece Georgiana went to Ramsgate last summer, I made a point of her having two men-servants go with her.

oewn-02209474-v.learner: to own something, or to keep it as yours.

oewn-00182551-v.learner: to put something with the things that are there, joining it to them and making them greater in worth, number, size, or reach.

oewn-00642490-v.learner: to put numbers together to make one number.
